instructions.task: In a chat where a persuader tries to get the other person (the persuadee) to donate to the charity Save the Children, tag the final 'Persuader message to tag' with the one persuasion strategy or dialogue act it uses.
notes: Tag only the final persuader message; the earlier chat is context to interpret it.
Messages are single sentences or fragments split from a longer turn; judge the function of this piece in context.

criteria.greeting: Opens the conversation or exchanges pleasantries: hello, hi, how are you, and answers to 'how are you' (I'm good, not bad).
criteria.source-related-inquiry: Asks whether the persuadee knows or has heard of Save the Children or what they know about it, or introduces the organization as the topic of the chat.
criteria.task-related-inquiry: Asks the persuadee's opinion, feelings or views on the task topic (what do you think of it, how do you feel about children's charities, does this sound like a good charity), asks what they are unsure about or whether they have questions or want more information, or poses a 'did you know' / 'have you ever thought about' question about children in need.
criteria.personal-related-inquiry: Asks about the persuadee's own life or past experience with giving: whether they have donated before, usually donate, volunteer, have children, which charities they support.
criteria.credibility-appeal: Builds the organization's credibility: facts about what Save the Children is and does, where it works, how long it has existed, what its programs achieve, its legitimacy, ratings and use of funds; the persuader vouching for the charity's quality or trustworthiness (even as a personal opinion, e.g. I really believe in them, they do important work); or pointing to its website and where to find information there.
criteria.logical-appeal: Reasons that the persuadee's donation is worthwhile: what their money would accomplish or buy, how much difference a donation makes, moral or rational arguments for why people should give. (Claims about what the organization itself does or has achieved are credibility-appeal.)
criteria.emotion-appeal: Tries to evoke sympathy, sadness, guilt or empathy: vivid descriptions of children suffering, starving, dying, in war zones, stories of particular children, imagining one's own child in that situation.
criteria.foot-in-the-door: Asks for or stresses a small, easy contribution as a first step: even a little helps, just a few cents, pocket change makes a difference.
criteria.proposition-of-donation: Directly asks or invites the persuadee to donate (would you like to donate, would you donate some of your payment) without asking for a specific amount.
criteria.ask-donation-amount: Asks how much the persuadee will donate, or suggests a specific amount for them to give.
criteria.donation-information: Explains how the donation works: it is deducted from the task payment, any amount from $0 to the full payment or whatever they are comfortable with, when and where they enter the amount, one-time or recurring options, and that the research team collects and sends it to the charity.
criteria.self-modeling: The persuader states their own donation or intention to donate (I will donate too, I give monthly), setting an example.
criteria.personal-story: The persuader tells an anecdote about their own life or experiences (places they have been, things they have seen or done).
criteria.praise-user: Praises or compliments the persuadee (you are generous, you are a good person, that's amazing of you).
criteria.thank: Thanks the persuadee or expresses appreciation for their help or donation (thank you, it's really appreciated, the children will appreciate it), including closing lines that contain thanks.
criteria.acknowledgement: A short affirmation or positive reaction to what the persuadee just said, with no content of its own: okay, yes, yes they are, absolutely, I understand, that's great, wow, this is true.
criteria.off-task: Talk unrelated to the charity or donation task (e.g. history, politics, unrelated chit-chat).
criteria.other: farewell: Says goodbye or wishes the persuadee a good day or night WITHOUT thanking them (have a great night, take care).
criteria.other: shared feeling: The persuader replies by sharing their own matching feeling, opinion or circumstance, or sympathising, rather than arguing for the donation or vouching for the charity: I feel the same, same here, I know what you mean, I can't imagine that either, I'm sorry to hear that, yes I have heard that, that's a good idea, so true.
criteria.other: answers about self: The persuader answers a question the persuadee asked about the persuader (where they live, whether they know the charity, what they do), other than stating their own donation.
criteria.other: confirm amount: Confirms, restates or checks an amount or decision the persuadee has already stated (so you are donating $10, right?; to confirm, 20 cents?), or bargains over a specific figure after the persuadee named one.
criteria.other: chat logistics: Talk about the chat or task itself rather than the rules of the donation: number of turns left, what the persuader is supposed to do, typos and corrections, payment methods or accounts (credit card, PayPal), offering to give details.
criteria.other: anything else: Anything else that fits none of the options: arguing with or criticising the persuadee, vague remarks, statements that use no persuasion strategy.
